ui.tagline: Reading the classics word by word
ui.motto: Every line Yikonglu has read aloud can be checked here.
ui.intro: Source text, page numbers in the base edition, the commentators' own words, pronunciation, our reading, and a public errata log, arranged book by book and chapter by chapter. Watch the videos on the platforms; come here to check.
ui.search_ph: Search the source text or a commentator's words
ui.p1: Source text and commentary are taken from woodblock editions; every citation carries its page, and the page image can be enlarged.
ui.p2: Whoever is quoted is named: Zhu Xi, Cheng Yi and Xie Liangzuo are kept apart; paraphrase is marked; nothing without a traceable source is posted.
ui.p3: When we got something wrong we record it: which episode, which line, what we said, what it is now, and why.
ui.by_chapter: Arranged by book and chapter. Base edition: Zhu Xi, Lunyu jizhu (Sibu beiyao printing).
ui.book_lead: Each chapter gives the source text, the key words in the commentary, what other commentators say, and Yikonglu's reading, with the video.
ui.cites_note: Every commentary line quoted in the video: the original wording, who said it, and the page in the base edition. “Paraphrase” marks our summary, not the commentator's words.

ui.rendering: Working English rendering by Yikonglu; the Chinese text above is what counts.
ui.errata_p1: Where Yikonglu misread or overstated something, the correction is logged here, newest first; old entries are never deleted. Only matters of content are recorded, not visual glitches.
ui.errata_p2: To report an error, email the address below with the episode, the line, your evidence, and the username you want credited. Entries are added after checking, credited to that username. You can also comment under any Yikonglu video.
ui.mail_note: The address is an image to keep spam robots away; please type it in.
ui.report: Found an error in this chapter? Email us; once checked, it goes on the errata page under your username:
ui.search_ph2: Type a few characters, e.g. 鸟数飞 or 孝弟
ui.search_none: Nothing found. Only chapters already read are indexed.
ui.about_p: Yikonglu is a channel that reads the Chinese classics word by word, chapter by chapter, using narrated animation and a small cast of recurring characters to bring one line of the text down to a real person in a real situation. It assumes you have not read the book and have not seen the earlier episodes.
ui.about_site: The videos on the platforms are for everyone; this site is for people who want to check. Every line Yikonglu has read aloud can be looked up here: the source text, its page in the base edition, the commentators' own words, the pronunciation, our reading; and whatever we got wrong is recorded on the errata page.
ui.about_c1: Source text and commentary are taken from woodblock editions, and each page names its base edition.
ui.about_c2: We give the commentators' reading before our own; our own view is labelled as Yikonglu's reading and never passed off as an ancient one.
ui.about_c3: Nothing without a traceable source is posted. Tell us about any error; corrections are public.

ui.follow_wx: Scan with WeChat to follow our official account; reply “目录” for the full contents.
ui.foot_src: Citations follow woodblock editions, named on each page. Tell us about any error; corrections are public.

1.1.title: Learning and practising it in season
1.1.yw: The Master said: To learn and, in season, to practise what you have learned — is that not a pleasure? To have friends come from afar — is that not a joy? To be unrecognised and yet not resentful — is that not what a gentleman is?
1.1.常见读法: You learned it, so review it on schedule.
1.1.字眼: “学之为言效也” — to learn is to imitate, to do as someone else does; “习，鸟数飞也” — xi is a fledgling beating its wings again and again; Xie Liangzuo: “时习者，无时而不习” — practising in season means there is no moment one is not practising (sitting like a corpse at a sacrifice, standing as if at a fast).
1.1.诸家: Cheng Yi also says “时复思绎”, to go over it in one's mind again and again; so the “review” reading is very old. Zhu Xi shifts the weight from the head to the body.
1.1.片里落点: What you learned, keep taking out to practise and to do. Today: watching the tutorial ten times is watching another bird fly.

1.2.title: Filial and fraternal duty as the root of ren
1.2.yw: Master You said: Those who are filial and fraternal yet fond of defying their superiors are few; those not fond of defying their superiors yet fond of starting disorder have never existed. The gentleman works at the root; once the root is set, the Way grows. Being filial and fraternal — is that not the root of ren?
1.2.常见读法: Filial and fraternal duty is the root of ren (humaneness).
1.2.字眼: “为仁，犹曰行仁” — wei ren here means practising ren; Cheng Yi: “谓之行仁之本则可，谓是仁之本则不可” — call it the root of practising ren, yes; the root of ren itself, no; “与者，疑辞，谦退不敢质言也” — the final particle yu marks a question, a modest refusal to assert.
1.2.片里落点: Filial and fraternal duty is where practising ren begins. Today: kind to strangers online, no patience for one's parents at home — that is starting from the far end.

1.3.title: Clever words and a pleasing face
1.3.yw: The Master said: Clever words and a pleasing face — rarely is there ren in them.
1.3.常见读法: Anyone who talks nicely and looks agreeable is a bad person.
1.3.字眼: “巧，好；令，善也” — literally both words mean something good; the fault lies in “致饰于外，务以悦人” — polishing the outside, working only to please; “圣人辞不迫切，专言鲜，则绝无可知” — the sage's wording is not harsh: he says only “rarely”, and we can tell he means “never”.
1.3.片里落点: Watch whether he does it to get the thing done, or only to be liked.

1.4.title: Three things I examine myself on daily
1.4.yw: Master Zeng said: Each day I examine myself on three counts. In acting for others, have I been less than wholehearted? In dealing with friends, have I been less than trustworthy? What was passed on to me, have I failed to practise?
1.4.常见读法: Reflect on yourself many times a day; zhong means loyalty to a person.
1.4.字眼: “尽己之谓忠，以实之谓信” — giving one's all is zhong, being true to the facts is xin; “传谓受之于师，习谓熟之于己” — chuan is what one receives from a teacher, xi is making it one's own; “三者之序，以忠信为传习之本” — in the order of the three, zhong and xin are the root of what is passed on and practised.
1.4.诸家: One reading in He Yan's Jijie takes chuan as what one passes on to others (teaching before one has mastered it); Yang Bojun reads san as “many times” rather than “three”.
1.4.片里落点: When you act for someone, did you hold anything back? Today: a colleague asks you to look over a plan; you can't be bothered to point out the flaw and say “looks good”.

1.5.title: Governing a state of a thousand chariots
1.5.yw: The Master said: To govern a state of a thousand chariots: be careful in affairs and keep faith; be sparing in expense and love the people; and call on the people's labour only in the right season.
1.5.常见读法: No common misreading; the question is why governing a state should be only these five things.
1.5.字眼: “道，治也” — dao here means to govern; “敬者，主一无适之谓” — jing (care) is keeping the mind on one thing and not wandering; “时，谓农隙之时” — the right season is the slack time in farming; Yang Shi cites the Changes: “节以制度，不伤财，不害民” — regulate by set measures, and neither wealth nor people are harmed.
1.5.片里落点: Cheng Yi: “此言至浅……若推其极，尧舜之治亦不过此” — the words are plain, but pushed to the limit, even Yao and Shun governed no differently. Today: a shopkeeper who keeps his word, doesn't waste money, and doesn't send staff on private errands in the busy season.

1.6.title: A young man at home is filial
1.6.yw: The Master said: A young man should be filial at home and fraternal abroad, careful and trustworthy, broadly loving toward all and close to the humane. If he has strength left over after that, let him use it to study the texts.
1.6.常见读法: Study comes last, and is optional.
1.6.字眼: “文，谓诗书六艺之文” — wen means the texts of the Odes, the Documents and the six arts; “余力，犹言暇日” — strength left over means spare time.
1.6.诸家: Cheng Yi and Yin Tun stress the root over the branches; Hong Xingzu pulls back with “文灭其质” and “质胜而野” — too much polish drowns the substance, too little leaves it rough; Zhu Xi: without study “无以考圣贤之成法……所行或出于私意” — one cannot check against the sages' established rule, and what one does may come from private whim.
1.6.片里落点: This is about order, not about choosing one and dropping the other. Today: the capable person who never studied has nothing to check himself against when he is wrong.

1.7.title: Honouring the worthy over good looks
1.7.yw: Zixia said: One who honours the worthy in place of beauty, serves his parents with all his strength, serves his ruler with his whole person, and keeps his word with friends — though people say he has not studied, I would certainly say he has.
1.7.常见读法: Several readings circulate online: valuing virtue over looks; choosing a wife for her virtue.
1.7.字眼: “贤人之贤，而易其好色之心，好善有诚也” — to prize a worthy person's worth and exchange one's fondness for beauty for it, is to love goodness sincerely; “致，犹委也……不有其身” — zhi means to hand over, to no longer keep one's person for oneself.
1.7.诸家: Yang Bojun reads the first clause as the husband-wife relation, completing a set of four; Wu Yu criticises Zixia: “其流之弊，将或至于废学” — pushed too far, this leads to abandoning study.
1.7.片里落点: Someone who never studied but does all this — Zixia says he has studied. Today: the elders who had only a few years of schooling.

1.8.title: A gentleman without weight has no dignity
1.8.yw: The Master said: If a gentleman lacks weight he will have no dignity, and what he learns will not hold firm. Make loyalty and trustworthiness your mainstay. Have no friend who is not your equal. When you err, do not fear to correct it.
1.8.常见读法: Only befriend people better than yourself (which sounds like social climbing).
1.8.字眼: “无、毋通，禁止辞” — wu is a prohibition; “友所以辅仁，不如己，则无益而有损” — friends are for helping one toward ren; one who is not up to you brings no gain and some loss; “惮，畏难也” — dan is to shrink from difficulty.
1.8.诸家: You Zuo strings the four clauses into one line: weight as the base — learning — loyalty and trust — the help of those who surpass you — correcting faults without fear; if you don't correct them, the worthy stop telling you.
1.8.片里落点: Zhu Xi takes the words as they stand and does not talk his way around them. Today: the one person willing to tell you to your face tells you twice; if you don't change, the third time he says nothing.

1.9.title: Care at the end, remembrance of the distant
1.9.yw: Master Zeng said: Take care over the end, and follow the distant dead with remembrance, and the people's virtue will return to fullness.
1.9.字眼: “慎终者，丧尽其礼；追远者，祭尽其诚” — care at the end means the full rites of mourning; remembrance of the distant means full sincerity in sacrifice; “终者人之所易忽，远者人之所易忘……厚之道也” — the end is what people easily neglect, the distant what they easily forget; attending to them is the way of fullness.
1.9.片里落点: Put your heart into the places that are easy to neglect and easy to forget. Today: driving two hundred kilometres to stand ten minutes at a grave.

1.10.title: Whenever the Master arrives in a state
1.10.yw: Ziqin asked Zigong: Whenever the Master arrives in a state he always hears about its government. Does he seek this, or is it given to him? Zigong said: The Master gets it by being warm, kind, respectful, frugal and deferential. The way the Master seeks it — is it not different from the way other men seek?
1.10.字眼: Each of the five virtues is glossed word by word (“良，易直也” — liang is easy-going and straight); “夫子未尝求之，但其德容如是，故时君敬信，自以其政就而问之耳” — the Master never sought it; his bearing being what it was, the rulers of the day respected and trusted him and came to ask him about their own government.
1.10.诸家: Zhang Shi: everyone wanted to listen, no one was willing to use him — “私欲害之，是以终不能用耳”, private desire got in the way, so in the end they could not.
1.10.片里落点: Coming to ask is not the same as handing you the job.

1.11.title: While the father lives, observe the son's intent
1.11.yw: The Master said: While his father lives, observe his intentions; after his father dies, observe his conduct. If for three years he makes no change to his father's way, he may be called filial.
1.11.常见读法: Even if the father was wrong, change nothing for three years.
1.11.字眼: “父在，子不得自专，而志则可知；父没，然后其行可见” — while the father lives the son cannot act on his own, but his intent can be known; after the father's death his conduct can be seen.
1.11.诸家: Yin Tun: “如其道，虽终身无改可也；如其非道，何待三年” — if the way was right, never change it; if it was wrong, why wait three years? You Zuo: it refers to “在所当改而可以未改者耳” — things that ought to be changed but can wait.
1.11.片里落点: What is wrong, change now; what can wait, let wait — that is time given to what one cannot bear to let go. Today: the small factory a father left behind.

1.12.title: In the use of ritual, harmony is prized
1.12.yw: Master You said: In the practice of ritual, harmony is what is prized. That is what made the way of the former kings beautiful, and they followed it in matters great and small. Yet there are cases where it will not do: to know harmony and seek harmony without regulating it by ritual — that will not do either.
1.12.字眼: “礼者，天理之节文，人事之仪则也” — ritual is the measured pattern of heavenly principle and the rule of human affairs; “和者，从容不迫之意” — he is composure without strain, not “being agreeable”; Zhu Xi: “严而泰，和而节” — strict yet at ease, harmonious yet measured.
1.12.诸家: Cheng Yi: “礼胜则离，乐胜则流” — too much ritual divides, too much music dissolves; Fan Zuyu: “礼之体主于敬，其用以和为贵” — the substance of ritual is reverence, its use prizes harmony.
1.12.片里落点: Harmony alone, with nothing to regulate it, does not work either. Today: the team where everyone only ever says “looks good”.

1.13.title: Trust that comes close to what is right
1.13.yw: Master You said: When a promise comes close to what is right, one's word can be kept. When respect comes close to ritual, one keeps shame and disgrace away. When one relies on those one has not lost closeness with, one can look up to them.
1.13.字眼: “信，约信也” — xin here is a pledge; “义者，事之宜也” — yi is what is fitting in the matter; “复，践言也” — fu is to carry out one's word; “皆当谨之于始而虑其所终” — all of these call for care at the start and thought for where they end.
1.13.片里落点: The work happens before you say yes. Today: agreeing at midnight, without a thought, to lend the money.

1.14.title: A gentleman does not seek to eat his fill
1.14.yw: The Master said: A gentleman does not seek to eat his fill or live in comfort; he is quick in action and careful in speech, and goes to those who have the Way to be set straight. He may be called fond of learning.
1.14.字眼: “志有在而不暇及也” — his mind is elsewhere and he has no time for it; “敏于事者，勉其所不足” — quick in action means pushing on where one falls short; “必就有道之人，以正其是非” — one must go to someone who has the Way to have one's right and wrong set straight.
1.14.诸家: Yin Tun cites Yang Zhu and Mozi as “学仁义而差者也” — people who studied ren and yi and went astray.
1.14.片里落点: Not going hungry on purpose; simply too occupied to mind.

1.15.title: Poor without flattery
1.15.yw: Zigong said: Poor without flattery, rich without arrogance — how is that? The Master said: That will do. But it is not as good as poor and joyful, rich and fond of ritual. Zigong said: The Ode says, “as if cut, as if filed; as if carved, as if polished” — is that what you mean? The Master said: Ci, now I can begin to discuss the Odes with you. Told what has gone before, you know what comes after.
1.15.常见读法: (The episode's question) Is “that will do” praise or dissatisfaction?
1.15.字眼: “凡曰可者，仅可而有所未尽之辞也” — “will do” always means barely adequate, with something still lacking; “未能超乎贫富之外” — not yet beyond poverty and wealth; “子贡货殖，盖先贫后富” — Zigong went into trade, poor first and rich later; “许其所已能，而勉其所未至” — the Master grants what he has achieved and urges him on to what he has not.
1.15.片里落点: Acknowledge what has been done, then push one step further. Today: from renting to owning without bowing or showing off — Confucius would say “that will do”.

1.16.title: Not troubled that others do not know me
1.16.yw: The Master said: Do not be troubled that others do not know you; be troubled that you do not know others.
1.16.字眼: Yin Tun: “君子求在我者” — the gentleman seeks what lies with himself; “不知人，则是非邪正或不能辨” — if you do not know others, you may fail to tell right from wrong, crooked from straight.
1.16.片里落点: The book opens with “unrecognised and yet not resentful” and closes here; the two ends meet.

2.1.title: Governing by virtue
2.1.yw: The Master said: One who governs by virtue is like the pole star: it stays in its place, and all the other stars turn toward it.
2.1.常见读法: The pole star does not move, so the ruler need do nothing at all.
2.1.字眼: “政之为言正也” — zheng (governing) means setting straight; “德之为言得也，行道而有得于心也” — de (virtue) means attainment, what one gains in the heart by walking the Way; “北辰……天之枢也” — the pole star is the pivot of the sky; “共，向也” — gong means to turn toward.
2.1.诸家: Cheng Yi: “为政以德，然后无为” — govern by virtue, and only then can one be without striving (the order cannot be reversed); Fan Zuyu: “所守者至简而能御烦” — what he holds to is utterly simple, yet it masters complexity.
2.1.片里落点: Not that decrees are unnecessary, but that the one who governs must first have gained something himself. Today: the form teacher whose word counts.

2.2.title: Thoughts without crookedness
2.2.yw: The Master said: The three hundred Odes can be covered by one phrase: thoughts without crookedness.
2.2.常见读法: All three hundred Odes are pure and innocent.
2.2.字眼: “蔽，犹盖也” — bi means to cover; “凡诗之言，善者可以感发人之善心，恶者可以惩创人之逸志” — in the Odes, the good lines stir a reader's good heart, and the bad ones chasten a reader's wayward will.
2.2.诸家: Cheng Yi: “思无邪者，诚也” — thoughts without crookedness means sincerity; Fan Zuyu: “知要则能守约” — knowing the essential, one can hold to what is concise.
2.2.片里落点: The “without crookedness” lies in the reader, not entirely in the poems. Today: a novel about a villain can still bring a reader round.

2.3.title: Guiding them by decrees
2.3.yw: The Master said: Guide them by decrees and keep them in line by punishments, and the people will stay out of trouble but have no sense of shame. Guide them by virtue and keep them in line by ritual, and they will have a sense of shame and, moreover, come right.
2.3.常见读法: Confucius was against laws and punishments.
2.3.字眼: “道犹引导，谓先之也” — dao means to lead, to go first; “政谓法制禁令” — zheng means laws, regulations and prohibitions; “苟免刑罚而无所羞愧……为恶之心未尝忘也” — merely escaping punishment without shame, the wish to do wrong is never gone; “格，至也” — ge means to arrive (another reading: to be set right).
2.3.诸家: Zhu Xi: “政者为治之具，刑者辅治之法，德礼则所以出治之本……虽不可以偏废” — decrees are the tools of government, punishments its auxiliary, virtue and ritual the root from which government issues; none can be dropped.
2.3.片里落点: Punishment and decree keep people from crime; virtue and ritual move them toward good. Today: the camera breaks, and the rubbish comes back.

2.4.title: At fifteen I set my heart on learning
2.4.yw: The Master said: At fifteen I set my heart on learning; at thirty I stood firm; at forty I had no doubts; at fifty I knew the decree of Heaven; at sixty my ear was attuned; at seventy I could follow my heart's desire without overstepping the line.
2.4.常见读法: A life timetable arranged by age.
2.4.字眼: “心之所之谓之志” — zhi (resolve) is where the heart goes; “于事物之所当然，皆无所疑” — no doubt about what things ought to be (no doubts); “天命……事物所以当然之故” — Heaven's decree is the reason why things ought to be so; “矩，法度之器” — ju is the carpenter's square, the instrument of measure.
2.4.诸家: Cheng Yi: “圣人未必然，但为学者立法，使之盈科而后进” — the sage was not necessarily like this himself; he sets out a rule for learners, so that they fill each hollow before moving on; Zhu Xi's own note: “因其近似以自名” — he named the stages by what they resembled.
2.4.片里落点: Not a certificate issued automatically at a certain age, but a road of learning.

2.5.title: Meng Yizi asks about filial piety
2.5.yw: Meng Yizi asked about filial piety. The Master said: Do not go against it. As Fan Chi was driving him, the Master told him: Mengsun asked me about filial piety, and I answered, “Do not go against it.” Fan Chi said: What did you mean? The Master said: While they live, serve them according to ritual; when they die, bury them according to ritual and sacrifice to them according to ritual.
2.5.常见读法: “Do not go against” = do whatever your parents say.
2.5.字眼: “无违，谓不背于理” — not going against means not turning one's back on what is right; “礼，即理之节文” — ritual is the measured form of what is right; Confucius explained it to Fan Chi “恐其失指，而以从亲之令为孝” — fearing the point would be missed and obeying a parent's orders taken for filial piety.
2.5.诸家: Hu Yin: “心虽无穷，而分则有限；得为而不为，与不得为而为之，均于不孝” — the heart is boundless but one's station has limits; failing to do what one may, and doing what one may not, are equally unfilial; Zhu Xi notes that the three great families were usurping rites at the time, “以是警之” — this was a warning to them.
2.5.片里落点: Today: borrowing money to throw a lavish birthday banquet is “doing what one may not”.

2.6.title: Meng Wubo asks about filial piety
2.6.yw: Meng Wubo asked about filial piety. The Master said: Parents worry only about their children falling ill.
2.6.字眼: Zhu Xi: “父母爱子之心……唯恐其有疾病” — a parent's love fears above all that the child will fall ill; so children should take their parents' heart as their own and take care of themselves.
2.6.诸家: Zhu Xi also records an older reading: “使父母不以其陷于不义为忧，而独以其疾为忧” — give your parents no cause to worry that you will fall into wrongdoing, so that illness is their only worry.
2.6.片里落点: Three readings of one line, side by side. Today: staying up all night drinking, riding without a helmet.

2.7.title: Ziyou asks about filial piety
2.7.yw: Ziyou asked about filial piety. The Master said: Filial piety nowadays means being able to feed one's parents. But even dogs and horses are fed. Without reverence, what is the difference?
2.7.字眼: “养，谓饮食供奉” — feeding means providing food and drink; “若能养其亲而敬不至，则与养犬马者何异” — if you feed your parents without reverence, how is that different from feeding dogs and horses; “甚言不敬之罪，所以深警之” — he states the fault of irreverence strongly, as a sharp warning.
2.7.诸家: Bao Xian (in He Yan's Collected Explanations): “犬以守御，马以代劳，皆养人者” — dogs guard and horses labour, so they too “feed” people; Hu Yin: “狎恩恃爱……渐流于不敬” — taking love for granted slides gradually into irreverence.
2.7.片里落点: Both readings land on reverence. Today: sending money on time, but sounding impatient on the phone.

2.8.title: Zixia asks about filial piety (the hard part is the face)
2.8.yw: Zixia asked about filial piety. The Master said: The face is the hard part. When there is work, the young take on the toil; when there is wine and food, the elders are served first — is that really all filial piety is?
2.8.常见读法: Whose face is the hard part?
2.8.字眼: “惟色为难” — only the expression is hard; “深爱者必有和气，和气者必有愉色，愉色者必有婉容” — deep love brings a warm air, a warm air brings a glad expression, a glad expression brings a gentle manner; “先生，父兄也” — “elders” means fathers and elder brothers.
2.8.诸家: An older reading: “承顺父母之色为难，亦通” — reading the parents' faces and complying is hard, also possible; Zhu Xi, from what follows, places it on the child's face. Cheng Yi on the four questions about filial piety: “各因其材之高下，与其所失而告之” — each was answered according to his ability and his failing.
2.8.片里落点: All the work was done; the face never arrived.

2.9.title: Hui is not slow
2.9.yw: The Master said: I talked with Hui all day and he never disagreed, as if he were slow. But when he withdrew and I looked at his private life, it was enough to bring out what I had said. Hui is not slow.
2.9.字眼: “不违者，意不相背，有听受而无问难也” — not disagreeing means taking it in without objecting; “私，谓燕居独处” — private means when at leisure and alone; “发，谓发明所言之理” — bring out means to make clear the principle spoken of.
2.9.诸家: Kong Anguo (in the Collected Explanations) takes it as Yan Hui explaining to fellow students; Zhu Xi quotes his teacher Li Tong: “默识心融，触处洞然” — silently grasped and dissolved into the heart, clear wherever it touches.
2.9.片里落点: Whether someone has learned shows outside the classroom.

2.10.title: Look at what he does
2.10.yw: The Master said: Look at what he does, observe what he goes by, examine what he rests content in. How can a person hide? How can a person hide?
2.10.字眼: “以，为也” — yi means doing; “观比视为详……由，从也” — observing is closer than looking; you means the way he goes by; “察则又加详矣。安，所乐也……则亦伪耳” — examining is closer still; an means what he enjoys, and without it the rest is false.
2.10.诸家: Cheng Yi: “在己者能知言穷理，则能以此察人” — one who understands words and fathoms principle in himself can use this to see into others.
2.10.片里落点: What he does, why he does it, whether he enjoys it. Today: leaving at six sharp the week the boss is away.

2.11.title: Reviewing the old to know the new
2.11.yw: The Master said: One who reviews the old and comes to know the new may be a teacher.
2.11.字眼: “温，寻绎也” — wen means drawing out a thread; “故者，旧所闻；新者，今所得” — the old is what one heard before, the new is what one gains now; “记问之学，则无得于心” — learning by memorising gains nothing in the heart.
2.11.诸家: Zheng Xuan reads wen as reheating cold meat.
2.11.片里落点: If you can only recite it, reheating it a hundred times still gives the same bowl.

2.12.title: The gentleman is not a vessel
2.12.yw: The Master said: The gentleman is not a vessel.
2.12.常见读法: A gentleman should be able to do everything.
2.12.字眼: “器者，各适其用而不能相通” — a vessel suits one use and cannot serve another; “成德之士，体无不具，故用无不周” — one of complete virtue lacks nothing in substance, so is useful everywhere.
2.12.片里落点: Virtue made whole first, then it can be used anywhere — not learning a hundred trades. Today: the accountant everyone likes to ask for advice.

2.13.title: Act first, then speak
2.13.yw: Zigong asked about the gentleman. The Master said: He first acts on his words, and then speaks of them.
2.13.字眼: Zhou Fuxian: “行之于未言之前……言之于既行之后” — do it before saying it, say it after doing it; Fan Zuyu: “子贡之患，非言之艰而行之艰” — Zigong's trouble was not that speaking was hard but that acting was.

2.14.title: Inclusive, not partisan
2.14.yw: The Master said: The gentleman is inclusive and not partisan; the small man is partisan and not inclusive.
2.14.字眼: “周，普徧也；比，偏党也” — zhou means all-embracing, bi means forming a faction; “皆与人亲厚之意，但周公而比私耳” — both mean being close to people, but zhou is public and bi private; “在公私之际，毫釐之差耳” — between public and private the difference is a hair's breadth.
2.14.片里落点: Same dishes on the table, different reasons for the dinner.

2.15.title: Learning without thinking
2.15.yw: The Master said: To learn without thinking is to be lost; to think without learning is perilous.
2.15.字眼: “不求诸心，故昏而无得” — not seeking it in the heart, one is in the dark and gains nothing (lost); “不习其事，故危而不安” — not practising the matter, one is unsteady and insecure (perilous).
2.15.诸家: Cheng Yi cites the Doctrine of the Mean — study widely, inquire closely, think carefully, distinguish clearly, practise earnestly: “废其一，非学也” — drop one and it is not learning.
2.15.片里落点: One is empty, the other hangs in the air. Today: bookmarking online courses without thinking vs. building theories without reading.

2.16.title: Working at strange doctrines
2.16.yw: The Master said: To work at strange doctrines — that is harmful indeed.
2.16.字眼: Fan Zuyu: “攻，专治也，故治木石金玉之工曰攻” — gong means working at something intently, as craftsmen work wood, stone, metal and jade; “异端，非圣人之道，而别为一端，如杨墨是也” — strange doctrines are not the sages' way but a separate end, like Yang Zhu and Mozi.
2.16.诸家: Cheng Yi held Buddhism to be the greater harm (a Song judgement about its own day); Liu Baonan's Correct Meaning records Sun Yi: gong = attack, yi = stop — the opposite meaning.
2.16.片里落点: Following Zhu Xi: burrowing into it is what does harm.

2.17.title: To know what you know
2.17.yw: The Master said: You, shall I teach you about knowing? To know what you know and to know what you do not know — that is knowing.
2.17.字眼: “子路好勇，盖有强其所不知以为知者” — Zilu loved daring and would force what he did not know into knowing; “无自欺之蔽，亦不害其为知” — free of self-deception, this does not stop it being knowledge; “况由此而求之，又有可知之理乎” — and seeking further from here, there is more that can be known.
2.17.片里落点: Admitting you do not know is where it starts.

2.18.title: Zizhang studies to gain office
2.18.yw: Zizhang was studying in order to gain office. The Master said: Hear much, set aside what is doubtful, and speak carefully of the rest — then you will make few mistakes. See much, set aside what is unsafe, and act carefully on the rest — then you will have few regrets. Few mistakes in speech, few regrets in conduct: office lies within that.
2.18.常见读法: Be a good person and you will be promoted.
2.18.字眼: “干，求也” — gan means to seek; “疑者所未信，殆者所未安” — the doubtful is what one does not yet trust, the unsafe what one is not yet sure of; Cheng Yi: “尤，罪自外至者也；悔，理自内出者也” — mistakes are blame from outside, regrets come from within; “凡言在其中者，皆不求而自至之辞” — “lies within” always means it comes unsought.
2.18.诸家: Cheng Yi raises the objection himself — “或疑如此亦有不得禄者” — some may do this and still not get office — and answers with “耕也馁在其中” — even farming can leave you hungry — and “惟理可为者为之而已” — simply do what is right to do.
2.18.片里落点: Confucius promises nothing; he turns seeking office into a lesson in being a person.

2.19.title: Raise up the straight
2.19.yw: Duke Ai asked: What should I do so that the people will submit? Confucius replied: Raise up the straight and set them over the crooked, and the people will submit; raise up the crooked and set them over the straight, and the people will not submit.
2.19.字眼: “错，舍置也” — cuo means to set in place; “凡君问，皆称孔子对曰者，尊君也” — whenever a ruler asks, the text says “Confucius replied”, out of respect for the ruler.
2.19.诸家: Cheng Yi: “举错得宜，则人心服” — when promotions and placements are right, hearts submit; Xie Liangzuo: “好直而恶枉，天下之至情也……然或无道以照之，则以直为枉、以枉为直者多矣” — everyone loves the straight and hates the crooked, but without a way to see clearly, many take the straight for crooked and the crooked for straight.
2.19.片里落点: The hard part is seeing who is straight. Today: promoting the people who only bring good news.

2.20.title: Approach them with dignity
2.20.yw: Ji Kangzi asked: How can I make the people respectful, loyal and eager? The Master said: Approach them with dignity and they will be respectful; be filial and kind and they will be loyal; raise up the good and teach those who are not able, and they will be eager.
2.20.字眼: “庄，谓容貌端严” — dignity means a grave bearing; Zhu Xi goes line by line: approach the people with dignity and they respect you; be filial and kind and they are loyal; raise the good and teach the incapable and they are eager.
2.20.诸家: Zhang Shi: “此皆在我所当为，非为欲使民敬忠以劝而为之也” — all this is what I ought to do anyway, not done in order to make the people respectful, loyal and eager.
2.20.片里落点: Ji Kangzi asks for a method; Confucius answers with duty. Treating duty as a method goes wrong again.

2.21.title: Why do you not take part in government?
2.21.yw: Someone said to Confucius: Why do you not take part in government? The Master said: The Book of Documents says: “Filial! Only be filial and a friend to your brothers, and extend it to government.” This too is taking part in government — why must one hold office to take part?
2.21.字眼: “定公初年，孔子不仕” — in the early years of Duke Ding, Confucius did not serve; “书，周书君陈篇” — the Documents here is the Jun Chen chapter of the Zhou Documents; “善兄弟曰友” — being good to one's brothers is called you; “推广此心，以为一家之政” — extending this heart makes the government of a household.
2.21.诸家: The punctuation of the quotation has always varied; Zhu Xi: “盖孔子之不仕，有难以语或人者，故托此以告之” — Confucius's reasons for not serving were hard to tell this person, so he answered with this — and also “要之至理亦不外是” — yet the deepest principle is no other than this.
2.21.片里落点: The words are a pretext, and the point is also true.

2.22.title: A person without trustworthiness
2.22.yw: The Master said: A person without trustworthiness — I do not know how he can manage. A large cart without its yoke-bar, a small cart without its collar-bar — how can they go?
2.22.字眼: “輗，辕端横木，缚轭以驾牛者” — ni is the crossbar at the end of the shafts, tied to the yoke for oxen; “軏，辕端上曲，钩衡以驾马者” — yue is the curved piece at the shaft end hooking the bar for horses; “车无此二者，则不可以行” — without these a cart cannot move.
2.22.片里落点: Without it, the ox is an ox and the cart is a cart; they never connect.

2.23.title: Can ten generations be known?
2.23.yw: Zizhang asked: Can ten generations hence be known? The Master said: Yin followed the rites of Xia; what it took away and added can be known. Zhou followed the rites of Yin; what it took away and added can be known. Whoever succeeds Zhou, even a hundred generations on, can be known.
2.23.字眼: “王者易姓受命为一世” — each change of ruling house receiving the mandate is one generation; “也，一作乎” — ye is written hu in one version (Lu Deming).
2.23.诸家: Ma Rong: “所因，谓三纲五常；所损益，谓文质三统” — what is followed is the three bonds and five constants, what is changed is form and substance and the three sequences (adopted by Zhu Xi, not Confucius's own words); Hu Yin: “因往推来” — inferring the future from the past; Zhu Xi: “非若后世谶纬术数之学也” — not like the prophecy and numerology of later ages.
2.23.片里落点: He watched two handovers and saw what stayed and what changed.

2.24.title: Sacrificing to spirits not one's own
2.24.yw: The Master said: To sacrifice to spirits not one's own is flattery. To see what is right and not do it is cowardice.
2.24.字眼: “非其所当祭之鬼” — spirits one has no business sacrificing to; “谄，求媚也” — flattery means currying favour; “知而不为，是无勇也” — knowing and not acting is lack of courage.
2.24.诸家: Zhu Xi says nothing about how the two lines connect; our own reading — “one does what should not be done, the other fails to do what should be done” — is marked as this video's reading, not Zhu Xi's.
2.24.片里落点: Taking gifts to the home of a boss you have nothing to do with; saying nothing in the meeting.

3.1.title: Eight rows of dancers in his courtyard
3.1.yw: Confucius said of the Ji family: Eight rows of dancers in his courtyard — if he can bear to do this, what can he not bear to do?
3.1.常见读法: “If this can be borne, what cannot?” = I can't stand it any more.
3.1.字眼: “佾，舞列也” — yi is a row of dancers; “天子八，诸侯六，大夫四，士二” — the Son of Heaven eight, lords six, ministers four, officers two (two accounts of dancers per row, “未详孰是” — unclear which is right); “孔子言其此事尚忍为之，则何事不可忍为” — if he could bring himself to do this, what could he not bring himself to do (ren = the Ji's hardness of heart); “或曰：忍，容忍也” — another reading: ren means to tolerate, given alongside.
3.1.诸家: Fan Zuyu: “降杀以两……不可以毫发僭差” — the ranks step down by two and must not be exceeded by a hair; Xie Liangzuo: “季氏忍此矣，则虽弑父与君，亦何所惮而不为” — if the Ji could do this, what would stop them even from killing father or lord?
3.1.片里落点: Four extra rows of dancers measure how hard a heart has become. Today: sitting in the boss's chair at the meeting.

3.2.title: The three families clear away to the Yong
3.2.yw: The three families had the Yong ode sung as the sacrificial vessels were cleared. The Master said: “Assisting are the lords; the Son of Heaven, solemn and grave” — what place do these words have in the halls of the three families?
3.2.字眼: “彻，祭毕而收其俎也” — che is clearing the vessels after the sacrifice; “天子宗庙之祭，则歌雍以彻” — at the Son of Heaven's ancestral sacrifices the Yong was sung while clearing; “相，助也；辟公，诸侯也；穆穆，深远之意” — xiang means assist, bigong the lords, mumu deep and grave; “讥其无知妄作，以取僭窃之罪” — mocking them for acting in ignorance and incurring the guilt of usurpation.
3.2.诸家: Cheng Yi traces it to the source: “成王之赐，伯禽之受，皆非也。其因袭之弊，遂使季氏僭八佾，三家僭雍彻” — King Cheng's grant and Boqin's acceptance were both wrong; that inherited fault led the Ji to usurp the eight rows and the three families the Yong.
3.2.片里落点: They didn't even understand the song they sang. Today: a corner shop's banner “Welcoming heads of state”.

3.3.title: A person without humaneness — what of ritual?
3.3.yw: The Master said: A person who is not humane — what has he to do with ritual? A person who is not humane — what has he to do with music?
3.3.字眼: You Zuo: “人心亡矣……礼乐不为之用也” — when the heart is lost, ritual and music do not serve him; Cheng Yi: “仁者天下之正理，失正理则无序而不和” — humaneness is the right principle of the world; lose it and there is neither order nor harmony; Li Yu: “礼乐待人而后行” — ritual and music depend on people to be carried out.
3.3.诸家: “记者序此于八佾雍彻之后，疑其为僭礼乐者发也” — the compilers placed this after the eight rows and the Yong, perhaps aimed at those usurping rites and music (the arrangement is a clue).
3.3.片里落点: Fill the eight rows, sing the emperor's ode — if the person is wrong, ritual and music can do nothing with him.

3.4.title: Lin Fang asks about the root of ritual
3.4.yw: Lin Fang asked about the root of ritual. The Master said: A great question! In ritual, rather frugal than extravagant; in mourning, rather grief than smooth arrangement.
3.4.字眼: “易，治也” — yi means arranged, as in tending fields; “节文习熟，而无哀痛惨怛之实” — the forms practised smoothly with no real grief; “礼贵得中……二者皆未合礼” — ritual values the mean, and both extremes fall short; “必先有质而后有文，则质乃礼之本也” — substance must come before form, so substance is the root of ritual.
3.4.诸家: Fan Zuyu: “祭与其敬不足而礼有余也，不若礼不足而敬有余也” — in sacrifice, better too little ceremony and enough reverence than the reverse; Yang Shi: “礼始诸饮食，故汙尊而抔饮” — ritual began with eating and drinking, with hollows for cups and hands for drinking; “周衰，世方以文灭质” — as Zhou declined, form was smothering substance.
3.4.片里落点: When both sides are off, lean towards the root. Today: a table full of dishes vs. a bowl of noodles.

3.5.title: The Yi and Di have rulers
3.5.yw: The Master said: The Yi and Di with rulers are not like the Xia states without them.
3.5.字眼: “亡，古无字，通用” — wang is the old form of wu, “without” (Wu Yu).
3.5.诸家: Cheng Yi: “夷狄且有君长，不如诸夏之僭乱，反无上下之分也” — even the Yi and Di have rulers and chiefs, unlike the Xia states in their usurpation and disorder, with no distinction of high and low; Yin Tun: “亡，非实亡也，虽有之，不能尽其道尔” — “without” does not mean they truly lack rulers, but that they have them and do not fulfil the role.
3.5.片里落点: The rebuke is aimed not at the Yi and Di but at his own people. Today: an old family firm where each branch keeps its own books.

3.6.title: The Ji sacrifice to Mount Tai
3.6.yw: The Ji family made the lu sacrifice to Mount Tai. The Master said to Ran You: Could you not save them from this? He replied: I could not. The Master said: Alas! Will it be said that Mount Tai knows less than Lin Fang?
3.6.字眼: “诸侯祭封内山川，季氏祭之，僭也” — lords sacrifice to the mountains and rivers within their realm; for the Ji to do so was usurpation; Ran You “时为季氏宰” — was then steward of the Ji; “救，谓救其陷于僭窃之罪” — save means save them from falling into the guilt of usurpation; “神不享非礼” — spirits do not accept improper offerings.
3.6.诸家: Fan Zuyu: “圣人不轻绝人。尽己之心，安知冉有之不能救，季氏之不可谏也” — the sage does not lightly give up on people; doing his utmost, how could he know Ran You could not save them or the Ji could not be admonished?
3.6.片里落点: It was the Ji who needed saving, not Mount Tai. Today: working for a boss you cannot talk out of it.

3.7.title: The gentleman does not compete
3.7.yw: The Master said: The gentleman does not compete — except, perhaps, in archery! Bowing and yielding, they go up; coming down, they drink. Even their competing is gentlemanly.
3.7.字眼: yin (drink) in the departing tone; “大射之礼，耦进三揖而后升堂” — in the great archery rite, pairs advance and bow three times before ascending the hall; “胜者乃揖不胜者升，取觯立饮” — the winner bows the loser up, who takes the cup and drinks standing; “其争也雍容揖逊” — their competing is composed, bowing and yielding.
3.7.片里落点: The target does not lie; what is contested is whether your own hand is steady.

3.8.title: The painting comes after the white ground
3.8.yw: Zixia asked: “Her artful smile dimpling, her lovely eyes clear, white to set off the colours” — what does this mean? The Master said: The painting comes after the white ground. He said: Then ritual comes after? The Master said: Shang, you have drawn me out! Now I can talk about the Odes with you.
3.8.字眼: “此逸诗也” — this is a lost ode; “素，粉地，画之质也；绚，采色，画之饰也” — su is the white ground, the substance of a painting; xuan is colour, its ornament; “后素，后于素也” — houxu means after the white; Kaogongji: “绘画之事后素功” — painting comes after the white work; “礼必以忠信为质” — ritual must have loyalty and trust as its substance; “起，犹发也” — qi means to draw out.
3.8.诸家: Xie Liangzuo: “子贡因论学而知诗，子夏因论诗而知学” — Zigong came to the Odes through learning, Zixia came to learning through the Odes; Yang Shi: “白受采……苟无其质，礼不虚行” — white takes colour; without substance, ritual does not work empty — and “玩心于章句之末，则其为诗也固而已矣” — fiddling with phrasing makes one's reading of the Odes rigid.
3.8.片里落点: If the ground is not smooth, every colour you put on comes out blotchy.

3.9.title: Not enough records
3.9.yw: The Master said: I can speak of the rites of Xia, but Qi cannot bear them out; I can speak of the rites of Yin, but Song cannot bear them out. That is because there are not enough records and worthies. If there were, I could bear them out.
3.9.字眼: “杞，夏之后；宋，殷之后” — Qi descends from Xia, Song from Yin; “征，证也” — zheng means to verify; “文，典籍也；献，贤也” — wen is written records, xian is worthy men.
3.9.片里落点: Confucius could tell it, but would not rest on his word alone. Today: grandmother's recipe — what's missing is the person standing at the stove.

3.10.title: The di sacrifice after the libation
3.10.yw: The Master said: At the di sacrifice, from the libation onwards, I do not wish to watch.
3.10.字眼: Zhao Boxun: “禘，王者之大祭也” — di is the king's great sacrifice; “成王以周公有大勋劳，赐鲁重祭……然非礼矣” — King Cheng granted Lu this great sacrifice for the Duke of Zhou's merit, yet it was not proper; “灌者……以降神也” — the libation brings down the spirits; “诚意未散，犹有可观；自此以后，则浸以懈怠” — while sincerity lasts there is something to watch; after that it slackens.
3.10.诸家: Xie Liangzuo links it to the previous chapter: “考之杞宋已如彼，考之当今又如此” — look to Qi and Song and it is like that; look to the present and it is like this.
3.10.片里落点: Looking back, the records and the people are gone; looking around, the rite is there but the heart is not.

3.11.title: Someone asks about the di sacrifice
3.11.yw: Someone asked about the meaning of the di sacrifice. The Master said: I do not know. One who knew its meaning would deal with the world as if looking at this — and he pointed to his palm.
3.11.字眼: “示，与视同” — shi is the same as “see”; “指其掌，弟子记夫子言此而自指其掌” — the disciples record that he pointed to his own palm as he said this; “非或人之所及也” — beyond what the questioner could reach; “不王不禘之法，又鲁之所当讳者，故以不知答之” — the rule that only kings perform di was something Lu had to avoid mentioning, so he answered “I do not know”; “岂真有所不知也哉” — did he really not know?
3.11.片里落点: Saying “I don't know” does not mean he didn't know.

3.12.title: Sacrifice as if present
3.12.yw: Sacrifice as if they were present; sacrifice to the spirits as if the spirits were present. The Master said: If I do not take part in the sacrifice, it is as if I had not sacrificed.
3.12.字眼: Cheng Yi: “祭，祭先祖也；祭神，祭外神也；祭先主于孝，祭神主于敬” — ji is sacrifice to ancestors, jishen to other spirits; ancestors call for filial piety, spirits for reverence; “此门人记孔子祭祀之诚意” — the disciples record Confucius's sincerity in sacrifice; yu (take part) in the departing tone; “此心缺然，如未尝祭也” — the heart feels the gap, as if one had never sacrificed.
3.12.诸家: Fan Zuyu: “有其诚则有其神，无其诚则无其神” — with sincerity there are spirits, without it there are none; “诚为实，礼为虚也” — sincerity is the substance, ritual the empty form.
3.12.片里落点: The form of the rite can be laid out by the book; the heart in it has to be brought by the one who sacrifices.

3.13.title: Better to court the stove
3.13.yw: Wangsun Jia asked: “Better to court the stove than the southwest corner” — what does that mean? The Master said: Not so. One who offends Heaven has nowhere to pray.
3.13.字眼: “媚，亲顺也” — mei means to ingratiate; “室西南隅为奥” — the southwest corner of the room is ao; “奥有常尊，而非祭之主；灶虽卑贱，而当时用事” — the corner has standing honour but is not the focus of sacrifice; the stove is lowly but holds power at the moment; “喻自结于君，不如阿附权臣也” — a hint that attaching oneself to the ruler is less useful than fawning on the powerful minister; “天，即理也” — Heaven is principle.
3.13.诸家: Xie Liangzuo: “圣人之言，逊而不迫” — the sage's words are modest and not pressing.
3.13.片里落点: Do the thing right and everyone is easy to deal with; do it wrong and being on good terms with anyone won't help.

3.14.title: Zhou looked to the two dynasties
3.14.yw: The Master said: Zhou looked to the two dynasties before it — how rich and refined its culture! I follow Zhou.
3.14.字眼: “监，视也” — jian means to look at; “言其视二代之礼而损益之” — it studied the rites of the two dynasties and took away and added; “郁郁，文盛貌” — yuyu means rich in culture.
3.14.诸家: Yin Tun: “三代之礼，至周大备” — the rites of the three dynasties were complete with Zhou.
3.14.片里落点: Following Zhou means following the work of improving on predecessors bit by bit. Today: the dishes at New Year's Eve dinner.

3.15.title: In the Grand Temple he asked about everything
3.15.yw: When the Master entered the Grand Temple he asked about everything. Someone said: Who says the son of the man from Zou knows ritual? In the Grand Temple he asks about everything. The Master heard and said: This is ritual.
3.15.字眼: “大庙，鲁周公庙。此盖孔子始仕之时，入而助祭也” — the Grand Temple is Lu's temple of the Duke of Zhou; this was probably when Confucius first took office and assisted at a sacrifice; “鄹人之子” — “son of the man from Zou” carries a slight; “敬谨之至，乃所以为礼也” — the utmost care is itself ritual.
3.15.诸家: Yin Tun: “礼者，敬而已矣。虽知亦问，谨之至也” — ritual is simply reverence; asking even when you know is the utmost care.
3.15.片里落点: Thirty years in, you still double-check.

3.16.title: In archery, piercing the hide is not the point
3.16.yw: The Master said: In archery, piercing the hide is not the point, because men's strength is not of the same grade. That was the way of old.
3.16.字眼: “射不主皮，乡射礼文；为力不同科，孔子解礼之意” — “piercing the hide is not the point” is from the village archery rite; “strength not of the same grade” is Confucius explaining it; “皮，革也……所谓鹄也” — pi is the leather target; “科，等也” — ke means grade; “古者射以观德，但主于中，而不主于贯革” — in old times archery showed virtue, aiming to hit, not to pierce.
3.16.诸家: Book of Rites: “武王克商，散军郊射，而贯革之射息” — after King Wu conquered Shang, armies disbanded and piercing archery ceased; “周衰……复尚贯革，故孔子叹之” — as Zhou declined, piercing was prized again, so Confucius sighed; Yang Shi: “中可以学而能，力不可以强而至” — hitting can be learned; strength cannot be forced.
3.16.片里落点: The contest is in what can be trained, not in what you were born with.

3.17.title: The sheep for announcing the new moon
3.17.yw: Zigong wanted to do away with the sacrificial sheep for announcing the new moon. The Master said: Si, you care about the sheep; I care about the rite.
3.17.常见读法: If only the outward form is left, why keep it?
3.17.字眼: gao read gu in Zhu Xi's note, gao today; xi read xi; “饩，生牲也。鲁自文公始不视朔，而有司犹供此羊” — xi is a live victim; from Duke Wen, Lu's rulers stopped attending the new-moon rite, yet officials still supplied the sheep; “爱，犹惜也。子贡盖惜其无实而妄费” — ai means to begrudge; Zigong begrudged the waste on an empty form; “然礼虽废，羊存，犹得以识之而可复焉。若并去其羊，则此礼遂亡矣” — though the rite had lapsed, with the sheep kept it could still be recognised and restored; remove the sheep and the rite is gone.
3.17.诸家: Yang Shi: “羊存，则告朔之名未泯，而其实因可举” — while the sheep remains, the name of the rite survives, and its substance can be revived.
3.17.片里落点: The sheep marks the rite; keep the marker and the rite can still be recognised and restored. Today: an old shop that makes one pot of the old recipe at the winter solstice, not for sale.

3.18.title: Serving one's lord with full ritual
3.18.yw: The Master said: Serving one's lord with full ritual, people take it for flattery.
3.18.常见读法: Do the courtesies in full and you get called a sycophant.
3.18.字眼: Huang Zushun: “孔子于事君之礼，非有所加也，如是而后尽尔。时人不能，反以为谄” — Confucius added nothing to the ritual of serving his lord; that was simply doing it fully; people of the time could not, and called it flattery; “以明礼之当然也” — this shows what ritual properly requires.
3.18.诸家: Cheng Yi: “若他人言之，必曰：我事君尽礼，小人以为谄。而孔子之言止于如此。圣人道大德宏，此亦可见” — anyone else would have said “petty men call it flattery”; Confucius stopped at “people”; the sage's breadth shows here too.
3.18.片里落点: Not a bit extra — ritual simply requires this; Confucius says only “people take it for flattery”, with no insult back. Today: getting to the meeting early and filling in expense forms fully, and being mocked as a try-hard.

3.19.title: The lord employs his ministers with ritual
3.19.yw: Duke Ding asked: How should a lord employ his ministers, and ministers serve their lord? Confucius replied: The lord employs his ministers with ritual; ministers serve their lord with loyalty.
3.19.字眼: “定公，鲁君，名宋” — Duke Ding, ruler of Lu, named Song; “二者皆理之当然，各欲自尽而已” — both are what is right, and each should simply do his own part fully.
3.19.诸家: Lü Dalin: “使臣不患其不忠，患礼之不至；事君不患其无礼，患忠之不足” — a lord should worry not that ministers are disloyal but that his own courtesy falls short; a minister should worry not that the lord is discourteous but that his own loyalty falls short; Yin Tun: “君臣以义合者也。故君使臣以礼，则臣事君以忠” — lord and minister are joined by what is right, so courtesy from above brings loyalty from below.
3.19.片里落点: Each side looks only at its own end; Duke Ding was the ruler, and his question was answered with his own half. Today: a team lead first asks whether people are treated with enough respect; the team member first asks whether the work is done properly.

3.20.title: The Guanju: joy without excess
3.20.yw: The Master said: The Guanju — joyful but not excessive, sorrowful but not hurtful.
3.20.常见读法: What is so good about a poem of unrequited love? Most people today read it only as a love song.
3.20.字眼: le read luo; “淫者，乐之过而失其正者也。伤者，哀之过而害于和者也” — excess is joy overflowing and losing its rightness; hurt is sorrow overflowing and damaging harmony; “关雎之诗，言后妃之德，宜配君子” — the Guanju speaks of the queen's virtue, fit to match a gentleman (Zhu Xi's reading, flagged here as his); “其忧虽深而不害于和，其乐虽盛而不失其正” — its sorrow is deep yet does not harm harmony; its joy is full yet does not lose rightness.
3.20.诸家: Zhu Xi: “欲学者玩其辞，审其音，而有以识其性情之正也” — he wants learners to savour the words, listen to the music, and so recognise rightness of feeling.
3.20.片里落点: Not too little feeling, but feeling full without going over. Today: crying while reading your wedding vows, wiping your eyes and finishing the last line.

3.21.title: Duke Ai asks about the altar of the soil
3.21.yw: Duke Ai asked Zai Wo about the altar of the soil. Zai Wo replied: The Xia used pine, the Yin cypress, and the Zhou chestnut (li), saying it would make the people tremble (zhanli). The Master heard and said: What is done is not discussed; what is accomplished is not remonstrated; what is past is not blamed.
3.21.常见读法: “What is past is not blamed” = let bygones be bygones.
3.21.字眼: “宰我，孔子弟子，名予” — Zai Wo, a disciple, named Yu; “古者立社，各树其土之所宜木以为主也” — in old times each altar was marked by planting the tree that suited the local soil; “战栗，恐惧貌……岂以古者戮人于社，故附会其说与” — zhanli means trembling in fear; perhaps because executions were once held at the altar he fabricated this; “非立社之本意，又启时君杀伐之心，而其言已出，不可复救，故历言此以深责之，欲使谨其后也” — not the altar's original meaning, and it invites the ruler to violence; since the words were out and could not be taken back, Confucius listed these to rebuke him severely and make him careful thereafter.
3.21.诸家: Yin Tun: “古者各以所宜木名其社，非取义于木也。宰我不知而妄对” — the altars were named after their trees, not for any meaning in the trees; Zai Wo did not know and answered recklessly.
3.21.片里落点: The three “nots” are not “never mind” but a heavy rebuke, to make him careful in future. Today: forwarding an unverified message in a group chat — the recall button only works for two minutes.

3.22.title: Guan Zhong's capacity was small
3.22.yw: The Master said: Guan Zhong's capacity was small indeed! Someone said: Was Guan Zhong frugal? He said: Guan had the Sangui terrace, and his officials held no double posts — how was that frugal? Then did Guan Zhong know ritual? He said: The ruler of a state has a screen at his gate, and Guan too had a screen at his gate; the ruler of a state, for meetings between two rulers, has a stand for inverted cups, and Guan too had such a stand. If Guan knew ritual, who does not know ritual?
3.22.常见读法: A man who helped make a hegemon had small capacity? Many take “small capacity” to mean frugal.
3.22.字眼: “器小，言其不知圣贤大学之道，故局量褊浅，规模卑狭，不能正身修德以致主于王道” — small capacity means he did not know the great learning of the sages, so his scope was narrow and shallow, unable to correct himself and bring his ruler to the kingly way; “三归，台名” — Sangui is the name of a terrace; “摄，兼也” — she means to hold concurrently; “屏谓之树” — a screen is called shu; “坫，在两楹之间……此皆诸侯之礼，而管仲僭之” — the dian stood between two pillars; all these were rites of lords, and Guan Zhong usurped them; “愚谓……虽不复明言小器之所以然，而其所以小者，于此亦可见矣” — though he does not say why the capacity was small, it can be seen from this.
3.22.诸家: Cheng Yi: “奢而犯礼，其器之小可知” — extravagant and breaking ritual, his small capacity is plain; Su Shi: “先自治而后治人” — govern yourself before governing others — “其本固已浅矣。管仲死，桓公薨，天下不复宗齐” — his foundation was shallow; once Guan Zhong and Duke Huan died, the world no longer looked to Qi; Yang Shi: “夫子大管仲之功而小其器” — the Master praised Guan Zhong's achievement and belittled his capacity. Note that the Xianwen book will praise Guan Zhong's achievement; the two are not the same matter.
3.22.片里落点: Confucius does not say outright where the smallness lies; it shows in the luxury and usurpation. Today: the company grows, the boss's office becomes a palace, and the rules apply only to others.

3.23.title: The Master speaks of music to the Grand Music Master of Lu
3.23.yw: The Master spoke of music to the Grand Music Master of Lu, saying: Music can be understood. At the start, all comes together; as it unfolds, it is harmonious, clear, and continuous, until it is complete.
3.23.字眼: yu read yù, da read tai, cong read zong in Zhu Xi's note and cong today; “时音乐废缺，故孔子教之” — music had fallen into disrepair, so Confucius taught him; “翕，合也。从，放也。纯，和也。皦，明也。绎，相续不绝也。成，乐之一终也” — xi is coming together, cong unfolding, chun harmonious, jiao clear, yi continuing unbroken, cheng the completion of one movement.
3.23.诸家: Xie Liangzuo: “五音合矣，清浊高下，如五味之相济而后和” — the five notes come together, high and low, light and heavy, like the five flavours balancing into harmony; “合而和矣，欲其无相夺伦” — together and harmonious, without crowding one another out; “不相反而相连，如贯珠可也” — not opposed but linked, like pearls on a string.
3.23.片里落点: First together, then harmonious, each part clear within the harmony, linked to the end. Today: a choir starts together, then blends, each voice part still audible, singing through in one breath.
